facts.quote: The top of the rotunda wall features a series of brick relieving arches , visible on the outside and built into the mass of the brickwork.
facts.statement: Brick relieving arches embedded in the rotunda wall help distribute structural loads.

facts.quote: The materials used in the concrete of the dome also vary. At its thickest point, the aggregate is travertine , then terracotta tiles, then at the very top, tufa and pumice , both porous light stones.
facts.statement: The dome concrete uses progressively lighter aggregates toward the oculus, from travertine through terracotta to tufa and pumice.

facts.quote: The 4,535-tonne (4,463-long-ton; 4,999-short-ton) weight of the Roman concrete dome is concentrated on a ring of voussoirs 9.1 metres (30 ft) in diameter that form the oculus, while the downward thrust of the dome is carried by eight barrel vaults in the 6.4-metre-thick (21 ft) drum wall into eight piers.
facts.statement: The Roman concrete dome transfers its downward thrust through eight barrel vaults in the thick drum wall into eight piers.

facts.quote: the downward thrust of the dome is carried by eight barrel vaults in the 6.4-metre-thick (21 ft) drum wall into eight piers.
facts.statement: The Pantheon drum wall is 6.4 metres (21 feet) thick.

facts.quote: The height to the oculus and the diameter of the interior circle are the same, 43.3 metres (142 ft)
facts.statement: The rotunda's interior circle has a diameter of 43.3 metres (142 feet).

facts.quote: The Pantheon in Rome is an example of Roman concrete construction.
facts.statement: The Pantheon is identified as an example of Roman concrete construction.

facts.quote: Hidden chambers engineered within the rotunda form a sophisticated structural system. [ 67 ] This reduced the weight of the roof, as did the oculus eliminating the apex.
facts.statement: Hidden chambers within the rotunda reduce roof weight as part of its structural system.

facts.quote: One example is the Pantheon , where the aggregate of the upper dome region consists of alternating layers of light tuff and pumice , giving the concrete a density of 1,350 kilograms per cubic metre (84 lb/cu ft) .
facts.statement: The Pantheon's upper dome concrete used alternating layers of lightweight tuff and pumice aggregate.

facts.quote: Roman concrete was based on a hydraulic-setting cement added to an aggregate .
facts.statement: Roman concrete used hydraulic-setting cement with aggregate.
